claim_summary: Amp stated Claude Opus 4.7 now powers its smart mode and reported an internal-eval score of about 72 percent versus about 65 percent for Opus 4.6; it warns vague prompts get narrower results.
availability: Vendor-stated default-model switch for a paid agent mode
limitation: Internal eval is unpublished vendor data, not an independent benchmark; model choice is a third-party (Anthropic) dependency that Amp changed again later in the window.

claim_summary: Amp announced a rebuilt remotely controllable, plugin-powered CLI with staged availability.
availability: first CLI piece rolled out; not the entire roadmap
limitation: Announced performance speed cannot be used as independent accepted-task outcome.

product: Amp CLI and TypeScript SDK packaging
claim_summary: Amp said the CLI ships as a single-file Bun-compiled executable and renamed npm packages @sourcegraph/amp to @ampcode/cli and @sourcegraph/amp-sdk to @ampcode/sdk, with old aliases to be removed on 2026-06-15.
feature: npm package namespace move away from Sourcegraph
availability: Vendor-stated rename; alias removal date stated in advance
limitation: Records the Sourcegraph-to-Amp namespace separation in distribution, not a legal ownership fact; npm registry metadata and alias removal on 2026-06-15 were not independently checked; executable-not-source packaging reduces inspectability for mirrors.

claim_summary: Amp announced Amp Labs: small teams of builders embedded with one company per industry and region under CEO mandates, profiting only through warrants if the partner's stock appreciates.
availability: Announced programme; partners not named at publication (later update links a Westpac partnership)
limitation: Business-model intent only; no delivered project, outcome or terms were verifiable from the page; the page was later edited to add a partnership update.

claim_summary: Amp announced Neo was available to everyone on May 27, after a staged May 6 CLI rollout; this is vendor-defined access, not measured reliability.
availability: Vendor claims broad CLI access on May 27, distinct from staged May 6 launch
limitation: Retain original May 6 preview row; do not backdate general availability or infer functional parity.

claim_summary: Amp said it can require active passkey authentication for certain operations such as remote-controlling a thread; workspace admins can enforce it and some privileged admin operations always require it.
feature: Passkey step-up auth for remote control
availability: Opt-in per user; admin-enforceable; renamed from sudo on 2026-06-25 per page update
limitation: Vendor-described control; phishing resistance, enforcement coverage and bypass paths were not independently tested.

claim_summary: Amp removed public internet-discoverable thread sharing, citing the difficulty of reviewing threads for sensitive file snippets as agents read more files; workspace and unlisted sharing remain; Amp says the change was not prompted by an incident.
availability: Feature removed (reversal of earlier public-sharing capability)
limitation: The 'no incident' statement is a vendor claim; unlisted unguessable-URL sharing still exposes content to anyone holding the link; reduces public corpus of agent transcripts available to researchers.

claim_summary: Amp reported thread control and monitoring across web/mobile/CLI.
availability: vendor states rolled out to everyone; independent account check pending
limitation: Access-control and parallel reviewer cost not independently evaluated.

claim_summary: First-party announcement of inspecting/staging code diffs for agent threads, including mobile review; does not validate reviewer accuracy
availability: vendor claim; see linked source
limitation: No independently reproduced task outcomes; reported launch scope, price/license/API and event date may differ from publication date; original 2026-10-12 first-party lead, independent factual QA pending

claim_summary: Amp launched orbs: Amp-hosted machines billed by the minute where agents run without supervision with the user's code, plugins and tools; changes can be reviewed, a terminal used and changes pulled locally via amp sync.
availability: Vendor-stated launch with per-minute billing
limitation: Isolation, data residency, network egress and cost per accepted task were not independently tested; the 2026-07-02 orb note (016-E04) is commentary on this launch, not a separate release.

source_title: Putting an Agent in an Orb
claim_summary: First-party discussion of headless remote execution design; no independent isolation or safety audit
availability: vendor claim; see linked source
limitation: No independently reproduced task outcomes; reported launch scope, price/license/API and event date may differ from publication date; original 2026-10-12 first-party lead, independent factual QA pending

claim_summary: Amp documented opt-in remote creation of threads on user-run hosts and headless runners.
availability: requires user-side runner/settings; broad production suitability unknown
limitation: Running agents in non-version-controlled locations and privilege scope requires review.

claim_summary: Amp replaced the smart, deep, rush and large modes with a low/medium/high/ultra effort dial and repackaged the deprecated modes as installable plugins with their exact prompts and tool lists.
availability: Vendor-stated replacement; old modes available only as plugins
limitation: Hides model identity behind effort levels, complicating reproducibility of agent runs unless the mode-to-model mapping is logged; claims about cost/capability trade-off are untested.

claim_summary: Amp said orbs can mint short-lived OIDC identity tokens (amp orb id-token) so cloud providers can grant scoped permissions without injecting secrets; tokens carry user and thread claims.
availability: Vendor-stated feature; relying-party configuration required
limitation: Token claims include user email per the example, a privacy consideration for audit logs; trust-policy scoping and token audience misuse were not independently tested.

claim_summary: Amp launched monthly subscriptions in beta alongside pay-as-you-go token pricing, saying it had until then priced only per token at API rates, and promoted linking a ChatGPT subscription and cheap open-weight models in its low mode.
availability: Beta pricing programme; tiers and prices on a separate mutable pricing page
limitation: Price levels were not captured; vendor cost claims are not a measured cost per accepted task; superseded in part by the 2026-09-13 free-tier change.

claim_summary: Amp said orbs can receive HTTP requests and wake on outside events such as GitHub CI failures, Linear issues, monitoring alerts or Discord messages, with examples like opening dependency-upgrade pull requests.
feature: Generic webhook triggers for remote agents
availability: Vendor-stated feature
limitation: Untrusted event payloads (issues, Discord messages) become agent input: prompt-injection, request authentication and replay controls were not tested; the 2026-10-12 GitHub-specific listener (CI2026-016-007) builds on this generic webhook support.

claim_summary: Amp announced that Amp Labs partnered with Westpac to change how the bank builds technology, with an Amp team working on site in Sydney on tasks such as migrating and modernising data systems.
availability: Partnership announced; outcomes not reported
limitation: One-sided vendor statement; Westpac's own confirmation was not opened in this pass; no delivered result, scope or contract terms verified.

source_title: Westpac and Amp Frontier to partner on AI engineering
claim_summary: Westpac's own release says it will partner with Amp Frontier Corporation, which will set up Amp Labs in Australia as a special purpose company with dedicated AI engineers working alongside Westpac teams; no financial terms disclosed.
availability: Partnership announced by the customer; outcomes not reported
limitation: Same partnership as CI2026-016-018 (not a second event); counterparty confirmation, not a neutral outcome evaluation; Westpac's date (Aug 7) is later than Amp's post (Jul 29); names the entity Amp Frontier Corporation rather than Amp Inc.; a Technology Decisions article the same day relays the release without independent analysis.

claim_summary: An Amp engineer wrote that Amp builds without pull requests and pushes to main, that while working toward SOC 2 its auditors accepted alternative change controls, that the criteria do not require human code review, and that the company is about 20 people.
feature: No-PR change-control process and SOC 2 preparation
availability: Process description; SOC 2 attestation status not stated as achieved
limitation: Self-described process and auditor reaction; no SOC 2 report or auditor statement reviewed; the headcount is a vendor statement; directly relevant to review-burden and accepted-quality constructs but not evidence of defect rates.

claim_summary: Amp said remote MCP servers (Streamable HTTP with OAuth or bearer tokens) can be connected on ampcode.com and used in orbs, the TUI, runners and Puck; MCP Apps, Resources and Prompts are not supported.
availability: Vendor-stated partial MCP support
limitation: Partial protocol support; token storage, per-workspace scoping and tool-permission behaviour were not tested.

claim_summary: Amp announced optional additional repositories in one orb project (up to 20); only primary repository automatic setup is stated.
availability: Provider-reported feature; access permissions and isolation untested
limitation: Secondary repo setup is not automatically executed; test cross-repo authorization, sandbox scope, secret isolation and task acceptance.

claim_summary: Amp said users can choose a verified Git name and email for commits made in orbs, managed with signing keys, and workspace admins choose whether commits use an Amp identity, each member's account or user choice.
feature: Configurable commit author identity and signing
availability: Vendor-stated feature with admin policy
limitation: Admin rules can attribute agent-written commits to a human or to Amp, which affects any repository-mining inference about AI authorship; signing-key handling was not tested.

claim_summary: Amp announced importance-based diff ordering in its review interface; improvements in actual defect detection or reviewer load are unmeasured.
availability: Provider-described interface feature
limitation: Not independent reviewer prioritization quality or a verified reduction in time or defects.

claim_summary: Amp said it is free when users bring their own compute (runners) and model subscriptions or keys, charging for hosted orbs, offering inference without markup, and formally extending its zero and minimal data-retention policy to all users; a 2026-09-30 page update widens BYOK options to every tier.
feature: Free Hobby tier and BYOK without Amp token fees
availability: Vendor-stated pricing change; page updated in place on 2026-09-30
limitation: Data-retention guarantee is a contractual vendor statement not independently audited; prices and tier limits live on mutable pages; costs shift to user-supplied compute and model subscriptions.

claim_summary: Amp said runners on user machines can create Git worktrees, directories and projects from the thread composer and can opt in (--amp-env) to receive the Secrets and Env Vars configured on ampcode.com.
feature: Runner worktrees and opt-in secret delivery
availability: Vendor-stated feature; secret delivery off by default
limitation: Delivering hosted secrets to user-run machines widens the secret-exposure surface; scoping and revocation were not tested.

source_title: Use Your Claude Plan in Amp
claim_summary: Amp said users can link a Claude Pro/Max subscription and select a Claude Code mode, which runs on the Claude Agent SDK instead of Amp's own agent while keeping orbs, runners, sharing and orchestration.
availability: Vendor-stated availability for everyone
limitation: Depends on a third party's subscription terms and SDK, which were not reviewed; the page contained a leftover authoring placeholder on 2026-10-16, a sign the post was edited after publication.

claim_summary: Amp announced subscriptions to GitHub PR comments, reviews and CI results for its agent threads via GitHub webhooks.
availability: Vendor-described opt-in thread subscription; not independently exercised
limitation: Webhook authorization, replay, secret management and prompt-injection review are untested. Do not permit auto-merge solely on agent feedback.
